text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.2% today after reporting quarterly earnings this morning, following a broader two-week slide of 11%. The decline fits a pattern seen across Big Oil refining stocks—while crude prices remain elevated, investor caution around earnings guidance has tempered enthusiasm, and crude itself fell again today as diplomatic hopes for resolving the Iran conflict reduced concerns about supply disruption.

Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with substantial oil and fuel inventories on hand, which limits pricing power for refiners even though global crude sits at $123 per barrel. The company also announced leadership changes recently, adding another layer of uncertainty as investors wait to see how new management will navigate what could be a softer energy environment if geopolitical tensions ease further.
